messages:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a pretty sharp latency cliff around the seqlen boundary on sm92 hosts. Profiling suggests the kernel chooser flips from our fused_fast_optimized path to the generic KV-cache path when seq goes from 128 -> 129 and kv_active is set. Observed ~2x tail latency for >128 tokens on small models. :eyes:

alex: probe dump (quick):
```
probe: sm=92 tc=1 bf16=1 fp8=0 kv_active=1 batch=1 seq=128 -> selected_kernel=fused_fast_optimized (p50 12ms p95 20ms p99 30ms)
probe: sm=92 tc=1 bf16=1 fp8=0 kv_active=1 batch=1 seq=129 -> selected_kernel=generic_kvcache_path (p50 22ms p95 45ms p99 68ms)
note: kernel-switch-count spike correlates with seq boundary
```

maria: damn. is that across all models or just small-llama variants?

alex: small-llama-7b and 3b so far. larger models take different kernel route (heads/seq combo) so they don't hit this exact flip. repro steps: `./bin/infer --model small-llama --seq 128 --repeat 1000` then bump to 129.

sam: looks like our chooser uses a pure seqlen threshold. it doesn't consider kv_active or batch. we should gate on kv_active + seq (and add hysteresis) so tiny jitter doesn't flip kernels repeatedly. quick idea:
```
seq_switch_up = 129
seq_switch_down = 120
if kv_active and seq >= seq_switch_up -> generic_kvcache_path
if seq <= seq_switch_down -> fused_fast_optimized
```
this prevents frequent oscillation around the boundary.

anya: +1 to hysteresis. also batch size matters a lot — at batch>1 fused path often remains better. so gating should be something like: (kv_active OR batch>1) AND seq>=129 => generic. Also log decision inputs (kv_active, batch, seq, sm, driver) with the kernel name so we can correlate.

alex: I'll add chooser instrumentation and a minimal hysteresis patch. pushing a canary to eng-runtime-dev, will attach traces. deploy-bot will kick the rollout.

deploy-bot: rollout/canary started for branch seqlen-hysteresis-fix -> 3 nodes in eng-runtime-dev. monitors: perf-latency, kernel-switch-count.

maria: when you post traces, include raw GPU profiler samples (warp occupancy, tensorcore usage). we need to see if tensorcore scheduling or driver heuristics changed.

alex: will upload perf traces in ~30m. opening an issue: https://redwood/issues/INF-2197 labeled perf-regression, priority P1 :pray:

sam: also run the kernel microbench (nvprof/cupti) on the exact sm92 driver (we saw driver 545 change scheduling earlier). microbench will show if fused kernel got deprioritized for larger seqs.

anya: fyi we had a similar flip last quarter after the bf16-packed kernel landed — could be an interaction with fp8 probe too. check the probe ordering for fp8/bf16 flags.

alex: good call, i'll include driver/kernel versions in the trace and the chooser logs. thanks everyone — i'll post updates in this thread once canary metrics come in.
